item.title: Scenarios for our Economic Future (12 minute read)
item.description: It is unknown yet whether AI will lead to unprecedented growth or widespread unemployment. Anthropic's Economics team built a model to understand how AI might affect jobs, growth, and unemployment in the US in the coming years. The model found that AI will lead to adverse impacts on wages and job prospects for knowledge workers in scenarios where growth is faster than anything in economic history, and in those scenarios, the challenge will be making sure wealth is broadly shared. The answer will depend on how AI affects all the tasks that make up the economy, the new tasks it creates, and how fast AI takes on this work.

item.title: The collection of good, fruitful open problems is now being mined in a non-renewable fashion (7 minute read)
item.description: Working out whether a question is actually worth working on is a lengthy, deliberate, and subjective process. Being aware of the difficulty landscape in a field is crucial in making such determinations. Every new advance in mathematics reduces the difficulty of solving problems, which reduces the difficulty landscape of the field. While there are an infinite number of possible problems to solve in mathematics, the vast majority of these problems are not worth focusing on. The indiscriminate use of powerful solution-extraction tools achieves the immediate short-term goal of solving problems at hand at the cost of sustaining the ecosystem for the next wave of progress, or in understanding the progress already obtained.

item.title: How well do agents use test/verification techniques? (68 minute read)
item.description: It's easier than ever to hit a particular quality bar by having coding agents use effective test techniques. However, software quality seems to be getting worse. This indicates that whatever defaults developers are using might not work very well. This study tests whether simple instructions to agents to use particular techniques or libraries improve implementation correctness. It found that agents tend to either just write the tests they would normally write, but inside a framework for a different type of test technique, or they'll use a technique superficially but not really do the things that get the value out of the technique.

item.title: The Curiously Playable Universe (41 minute read)
item.description: A domain becomes playable when enough of its complexity can be compressed into a state where there is some reasonably stable repertoire of actions, interactions can be repeated, outcomes provide feedback about better and worse play, and the environment is stationary enough that lessons learned yesterday remain useful tomorrow. None of these conditions need to be perfect, as playability is a matter of degree. Far more of reality than we have previously expected can be turned into a game. Once something can be turned into a game, then it's possible to create a system that can beat it.

item.description: Meta has released a new model with capabilities close to top competitors. Developers can now access and pay for Muse Spark 1.3. The model will soon roll out to Meta's social media platforms. Meta has yet to decide whether to release the model's weights. It still plans to release weights for the prior version, Muse Spark 1.2.

item.title: Google releases Gemini 3.8 Flash, its third Flash model in six weeks (3 minute read)
item.description: Google has released its third Flash model in just six weeks in two variations. The standard model is good for agentic tasks and software development, while the Cyber model has been tuned for vulnerability detection and mitigation. The Cyber model is currently limited to trusted testers and governments. API access to the model is available at an introductory rate of $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens through until the end of the year.

item.title: The race to engineer new knobs for the human brain (17 minute read)
item.description: Chemogenetics is a powerful technique that modifies specific neurons so they can be controlled remotely by normally inert drugs. There are several ongoing clinical trials of chemogenetics in China. The research could result in new ways of treating epilepsy, Parkinson's disease, and pain. This post looks at chemogenetics, describes what those first clinical trials are doing, and looks at how they could be improved upon.

item.title: Robotaxis Try Their Luck on London's Medieval Roads (3 minute read)
item.description: The arrival of 15 robotaxis in London is an important step for the autonomous vehicle industry. Acceptance of the technology has been slower in European cities, where the driving environment can be complex, and regulation is stiff. The failure rate of a driver's license test in London is just over 50%. 15 cars will be available for ride-hailing through Uber's app during the safety testing period.

item.title: How we make AI coding more cost efficient without sacrificing task quality (14 minute read)
item.description: Token count alone isn't a meaningful measure of efficiency. The goal should be to use the right amount of context to move a task forward. Concise tool responses can sometimes require additional calls or work if they leave out information agents need. This ultimately makes tasks slower and more expensive, which is why it is important to optimize for the outcome rather than the tool call.

item.title: AI Productivity Doesn't Mean What I Think It Means (5 minute read)
item.description: One-shot prompt templates often fail. The current best working architecture is a closed-loop taste flywheel. AI raises the ceiling of what the same effort produces. Users should push for the higher-quality output AI now makes possible rather than just accepting the pre-AI baseline.

item.title: In a Big Win, Google Avoids a Breakup of Its Ad Tech Business (3 minute read)
item.description: A federal judge has ruled that Google must make changes to its advertising business but will not have to break it up. The ruling will ensure that Google's power over the internet will remain largely unchanged. Google has been ordered to change its business practices to benefit competitors, but no specific instructions have been provided. The ruling is another sign that the federal government's attempts to rein in the power of big tech have faltered.

item.title: How to protect yourself from workslop (3 minute read)
item.description: Workslop is when your co-workers or managers communicate via big chunks of copy-pasted AI-generated text. The core problem with workslop is that the effort involved is asymmetrical. It costs almost no effort to produce slop, but it still costs effort to read. This post looks at different ways to handle this workslop so that you don't waste ten minutes of effort for every ten seconds of theirs.
